p: gold become dim: By the gold he means the princes, as by the stones he understands the priests.
pitchers: Which are of small value and have no honour.
draw out the breast: Though the dragons are cruel, yet they pity their young, and nourish them, which Jerusalem does not do.
ostriches in the wilderness: The women forsake their children as the ostrich does her eggs, Job 39:17.
visage is blacker than a coal: They who were before most in God's favour are now in greatest abomination to him.
fruits of the field: For lack of food they pine away and consume.
her: He means that these things are come to pass therefore, contrary to all men's expectations.
in the streets: Some refer this to the blind men who as they went, stumbled on the blood, of which the city was full.
men could not touch their garments: Meaning the heathen who came to destroy them could not abide them.
they respected not the persons of: That is, the enemies.
a nation that could not save: He shows two principal causes for their destruction: their cruelty and their vain confidence in man: for they trusted in the help of the Egyptians.
breath of our nostrils: Our king Josiah, in whom stood our hope of God's favour and on whom depended our state and life was slain, whom he calls anointed, because he was a figure of Christ.
O daughter of Edom: This is spoken by derision.
will no more carry thee away: He comforts the Church because after seventy years their sorrows will have an end while the wicked would be tormented for ever.
